title: Hindsight is 20/20: Building Agent Memory that Retains, Recalls, and Reflects
by: Chris Latimer, Nicolo Boschi, Chris Bartholomew (Vectorize.io), Andrew Neeser (The Washington Post), Gaurav Srivastava, Xuan Wang, Naren Ramakrishnan (Virginia Tech), December 2025. Id and title verified. Read in full from the arXiv PDF (v1), body only; appendix prompts skimmed.
summary: Hindsight keeps an agent's memory in four separate networks: world facts, the agent's own experiences, opinions (with a confidence score) and observations (neutral summaries of an entity). Three operations work on it: retain (store), recall (search within a token budget) and reflect (answer and update opinions). Facts are extracted as a few self-contained narratives per conversation, each with when it happened and when it was mentioned. It reports 83.6% to 91.4% on LongMemEval and 83.2% to 89.6% on LoCoMo depending on the model.
ideas: Keep evidence and belief apart: world and experience facts are evidence, opinions are beliefs with confidence, observations are summaries, each stored in its own network.
Each memory has three times: the start and end of when the event happened, and when it was mentioned; a time-bounded query keeps only memories whose interval overlaps it.
Narrative extraction: 2 to 5 self-contained facts per conversation instead of many small fragments, so meaning does not depend on how the text was cut.

Opinion update is a fixed rule once a model has labelled the evidence: reinforce adds a step, weaken subtracts one, contradict subtracts two, neutral changes nothing; the text may be rewritten on strong contradiction.
Observations (entity summaries) are rebuilt in the background whenever new facts about that entity arrive, so writes stay fast.

The agent's background is merged by a model that resolves conflicts in favour of the new information, overwriting the old (born in Colorado becomes born in Texas) with no history of the old value described.
Recall runs four searches (vector, keyword BM25, graph spreading, time range), fuses them by rank and reranks, then fills up to a caller-given token budget.

Caveats: baseline numbers are copied from other reports (Supermemory's for LongMemEval, Backboard's for LoCoMo) that used a GPT-4o judge, while Hindsight was judged by GPT-OSS-120B; the token budgets are left as '<add>' placeholders in the text; the authors build the product.

took.idea: Keep evidence apart from belief: raw docs stay as written, derived docs say they are derived and cite what they rest on
A when-it-happened interval separate from a when-it-was-written time
A model may label the relation, but a fixed rule applies the change
Reads take a budget and return the best docs that fit
Compare systems only under the same judge, and say who ran each baseline
